docs.title: vexy-co-model-catalog
docs.text: vexy-co-model-catalog downloads the list of available models from AI providers, writes each list to disk in a stable, sorted form, and keeps track of which providers answered and which failed. It ships a command-line tool, vmc (also installed as vexy-model-catalog), and a Python package, vexy_co_model_catalog.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
You give the tool a provider name, for example openai, and an API key in the environment variable that provider expects, for example OPENAI_API_KEY.

The tool then:

  1. Looks up the provider in its built-in table of 40 providers. The table holds the provider type, the API key variable and the variable that holds the base URL.
  2. Sends one GET request to <base URL>/models with the right authentication header (Authorization: Bearer … for OpenAI-compatible APIs, x-api-key for Anthropic).
  3. Sorts the response by model ID.
  4. Writes two files into the current directory:
    • config/json/models_openai.json — the full response, sorted.
    • config/txt/models_openai.txt — one model ID per line.
  5. Records the result in models/extra/failed_providers.json, so a later run can skip providers that are failing.
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
vmc fetch openai

✓ openai: <N> models

Fetch Complete: 1 successful, 0 failed, 0 skipped

<N> is the number of model IDs the provider returned.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• People who maintain configuration for several LLM command-line tools and want a current list of model IDs per provider.
  • Scripts that need a local, versionable snapshot of what each provider offers.
  • Users of the older dump_models.py script, which this package replaces. The file names (models_<provider>.json, models_<provider>.txt) are the same.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The package is versioned from git tags (v1.0.0 to v1.0.4 exist) and is not yet published on PyPI. Until it is, install it from the GitHub repository; see Installation.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: The command is vmc; vexy-model-catalog and python -m vexy_co_model_catalog run the same program. Every command below is a method of the CLI class in src/vexy_co_model_catalog/cli.py, exposed through Python Fire.

docs.title: How arguments work
docs.text:
Fire maps method arguments to the command line:

  • A positional argument can be given by position or by name: vmc fetch openai and vmc fetch --providers=openai are the same.
  • A boolean flag is switched on by its name alone: --force. Switch a flag that defaults to on off with --no<name>, for example --nooutput_txt.
  • Flag names use underscores, as in the source: --max_concurrency, --only_successful.

  • To see the flags of one command without running it, put -- before --help:

    vmc fetch -- --help

    Without the --, Fire passes --help to the command, which fails.

Comma-separated lists need extra quotes

Fire turns an unquoted openai,groq into a tuple, and the commands that take a provider list expect a string. Wrap the list in a second pair of quotes:

vmc fetch --providers='"openai,groq"'
vmc validate '"openai,groq"'

A single provider name needs no extra quotes.

Running vmc with no command prints the list of commands.

docs.title: providers
docs.text:
Show the built-in provider table, or one provider.

vmc providers                 # table of all providers
vmc providers show openai     # one provider
Argument Default Meaning action list list, show, add or remove name "" Provider name for show, add, remove

The table has the columns Name, Type, Status, API Key Env and Base URL. Status is Failed when the failure tracker has the provider marked as failed, otherwise Ready; a key symbol follows when the API key variable is set.

add and remove only print Provider management is currently read-only. The provider list is defined in code; see Providers.

Aliases: ls, list.

docs.title: fetch
docs.text:
Download model lists and write them to disk.

vmc fetch                                  # every provider
vmc fetch groq                             # one provider
vmc fetch --providers='"openai,groq"'      # several providers
vmc fetch groq --force                     # overwrite existing files
vmc fetch --legacy_output                  # write to models/json and models/text
Flag Default Meaning --providers, -p "" Provider names, comma-separated. Empty or all means every provider. --max_concurrency, -m 8 Maximum concurrent requests. --force, -f off Fetch even when both output files already exist. --output_json on Write the JSON response. --output_txt on Write the list of model IDs. --output_config off Also generate per-provider config files for aichat, codex and mods. --only_successful off Skip providers the failure tracker has marked as failed. --legacy_output, -l off Use the models/json/ and models/text/ layout instead of config/json/ and config/txt/.

What happens, in order:

  1. The provider names are resolved against the built-in table. Unknown names print Warning: Provider '<name>' not found.
  2. With --only_successful, providers marked as failed are removed.
  3. Each provider is validated (API key variable set, base URL present). Invalid providers are listed with guidance and removed from the run.
  4. For each remaining provider: if both output files exist and --force is off, it is skipped. Otherwise the tool requests the model list, sorts it, extracts the model IDs and writes the files.
  5. A summary line reports how many providers succeeded, failed and were skipped.

Failed requests are retried. Authentication errors (401, 403), rate limits (429) and other HTTP errors mark the provider as failed in the failure tracker.

Successful responses go into the model cache with a time-to-live of two hours (openai, anthropic, groq) or one hour (all others). The cache keeps its files in .cache/vexy_model_catalog/. vmc cache reports on it and clears it.

Aliases: get, dl, download, sync.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Check provider configuration without sending requests.

vmc validate            # all providers
vmc validate openai
Argument Default Meaning providers all Provider names, comma-separated, or all.

For each provider the output is Valid, Valid with warnings or INVALID, with the issues found and guidance such as where to get a key. A summary gives the totals and the success rate.

Aliases: check, test, verify.

docs.title: provider_health
docs.text:
Send a request to each provider's endpoint and classify it as healthy, degraded or unhealthy.

vmc provider_health groq --timeout=5
Argument Default Meaning providers all Provider names, comma-separated, or all. timeout 10.0 Request timeout in seconds.

docs.title: stats
docs.text:
Count the files the tool has written and summarise provider reliability.

vmc stats

System Statistics

Storage:
  Config JSON files: 1
  Config TXT files: 1
  Aichat configs: 0
  Codex configs: 0
  Mods configs: 0

Provider Reliability:
  Total tracked: 1
  Currently working: 1
  Currently failed: 0
  Overall success rate: 100.0%

Aliases: st, status.

docs.title: clean
docs.text:
Remove files the tool created.

vmc clean --temp       # leftover .*.tmp files from interrupted writes
vmc clean --configs    # generated models_* files in config/aichat, config/codex, config/mods
vmc clean --failed     # reset the failure tracker

With no flag the command prints Specify what to clean: --temp, --configs, or --failed. --configs does not touch config/json/ or config/txt/.

Aliases: rm, clear, remove.

docs.title: link
docs.text:
Create symbolic links (or copies) to the fetched files in one flat directory.

vmc link                                   # link every provider into models/
vmc link --target_dir=~/models --copy_files
vmc link --providers=openai
Flag Default Meaning --target_dir, -t models Directory to put the links or copies in. Created if missing. --source_dir, -s config Source layout. config reads config/json/ and config/txt/. --copy_files, -c off Copy the files instead of linking. --providers, -p "" Provider names; empty or all means every provider that has files.

An existing file or link with the same name in the target directory is replaced.

docs.title: migrate
docs.text:
Run the assistant that inspects dump_models.py output and suggests a migration plan. See Migrating from dump_models.py.

vmc migrate

The assistant is the script scripts/migrate_from_dump_models.py, which is not part of the installed package. The command only works from a source checkout; otherwise it prints Migration script not found.

docs.title: health
docs.text:
Run the built-in health checks: system resources, storage, network connectivity, configuration, dependencies and providers. The result is an overall status of healthy, warning, critical or unknown, followed by the issues found per component.

vmc health
vmc health --detailed      # include system metrics
vmc health --fix           # attempt safe automatic fixes

Aliases: diag, diagnostics, healthcheck.

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
Inspect or clear the response cache.

vmc cache                                # statistics (action defaults to stats)
vmc cache invalidate --provider=openai
vmc cache clear --provider=openai
vmc cache clear --clear_all
Argument Default Meaning action stats stats, clear or invalidate --provider "" Provider to target --clear_all off With clear: empty every cache

docs.title: completion
docs.text:
Print a shell completion script.

vmc completion bash
vmc completion zsh --install    # print installation instructions instead

Supported shells: bash, zsh, fish.

docs.title: Other commands
docs.text:
These commands exist and run, but they report on the tool's own monitoring subsystems rather than on model catalogs.

Command Arguments What it does version — Print the package version. help — Print an overview of commands with examples. Some examples in this overview name commands that do not exist in this version (generate-configs, backup-configs, restore-configs). aliases — Print the table of command aliases. setup_wizard — Interactive first-run wizard that walks through API key setup. It asks questions, so run it in a terminal. validate_config config_path, tool_name="" Check the syntax of an aichat, codex or mods config file. The tool is guessed from the path when tool_name is empty. validate_models file_path, provider_name="" Validate a saved provider response, such as config/json/models_openai.json. rate_limits provider="all" Show the rate limiter's statistics. show_analytics --show (on), --disable Show local usage analytics, or disable collection. performance action="stats", --save, --clear Show or manage stored performance metrics. Actions: stats, history, save, clear. integrity action="report", --verify_all, --repair, --cleanup_days=30 Checksums of tracked files. Actions: report, verify, cleanup. monitor action="dashboard", --export, --start, --stop Monitoring dashboard. Actions: dashboard, metrics, alerts, trends, export. monitoring_status — Show the monitoring system's status. production_status — Show deployment status. production_init — Turn on production-mode error handling and logging. production_readiness — Check deployment readiness. production_errors — Summarise recorded errors. production_diagnostics level="standard", --auto_fix Diagnostics at level basic, standard, enterprise or critical. production_health_advanced --continuous, --interval=300 Health checks, optionally repeated every interval seconds until Ctrl+C. cli_performance, optimization_info — Show the CLI's start-up optimisation data.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: A provider that fails or is unknown does not change the exit status: vmc fetch nosuchprovider prints a warning and exits with 0. An unknown command or a malformed argument makes Fire exit with 2. When you script around vmc, check the printed summary or the failure tracker file described in Output files.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: vmc has no configuration file. It is controlled by environment variables and by the directory you run it from.

docs.title: API keys and base URLs
docs.text:
Each provider reads one variable for its API key and one for its base URL. The names are listed in Providers. Set them in your shell profile or export them before a run:

export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
export GROQ_API_KEY="..."

A provider whose key variable is empty fails validation and is left out of the run. The litellm provider needs no key.

docs.title: Tool behaviour variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Effect VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED true Write a usage record for every run into analytics/. Set to false, 0 or no to turn it off. VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED true Run the performance monitor, which keeps data in performance/. Set to false to turn it off; vmc performance then prints a notice instead. VEXY_MEMORY_PROFILING false With true, the performance monitor also records memory snapshots. VEXY_DETAILED_PROFILING false With true, the performance monitor records detailed counters. VMC_PRODUCTION_MODE false With true, yes or 1, every run starts production-mode error handling and file logging. VMC_LOG_DIR see below Directory for production-mode log files. VMC_LOG_LEVEL INFO Console log level in production mode.

Values are compared case-insensitively. VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED and VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED accept true, 1 or yes as on.

Without VMC_LOG_DIR, production-mode logs go to:

Platform Directory macOS ~/Library/Logs/vexy-co-model-catalog Windows ~/AppData/Local/vexy-co-model-catalog Linux and other Unix systems ~/.local/share/vexy-co-model-catalog/logs

docs.title: Files written to the working directory
docs.text:
Every vmc command creates the CLI object first, and that step already touches the working directory. Running even vmc providers in a directory can leave these behind:

Path Purpose How to avoid it analytics/analytics_<date>_<time>_<id>.json One usage record per run VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false performance/ Performance monitor data VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED=false .cache/vexy_model_catalog/ Response cache —

A usage record looks like this. It stays on your machine; the analytics module makes no network requests.

The catalog files themselves (config/, models/) are described in Output files.

docs.title: A clean setup for scheduled runs
docs.text:
To refresh catalogs on a schedule without collecting analytics or performance data:

  1. Pick a directory for the catalogs, for example ~/model-catalog.

  2. Create a script ~/model-catalog/refresh.sh:

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd ~/model-catalog
export VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false
export VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED=false
vmc fetch --force --only_successful

  3. Make it executable with chmod +x ~/model-catalog/refresh.sh.

  4. Add it to cron or another scheduler.

The script needs the API keys in its environment. cron does not read your interactive shell profile, so export the keys in the script or in a file the script sources.

--only_successful skips providers that failed last time. Run vmc clean --failed now and then so those providers get another try.

docs.title: Response cache
docs.text:
Successful responses are cached with a time-to-live of two hours for openai, anthropic and groq and one hour for all other providers. Manage the cache with vmc cache:

vmc cache                           # statistics
vmc cache clear --provider=openai   # drop entries for one provider
vmc cache clear --clear_all         # drop everything

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Content src/vexy_co_model_catalog/ The package src/vexy_co_model_catalog/cli.py The CLI class behind vmc src/vexy_co_model_catalog/core/provider.py Provider table and ProviderConfig src/vexy_co_model_catalog/core/fetcher.py ModelFetcher, the HTTP side src/vexy_co_model_catalog/core/storage.py StorageManager, atomic file writes src/vexy_co_model_catalog/core/config.py aichat, codex and mods snippet generators tests/ pytest suite scripts/ Helper scripts, including the migration assistant external/ The original dump_models.py and saved outputs, for comparison src_docs/ Documentation source (this site) docs/ The built documentation site, served by GitHub Pages

docs.title: Set up an environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and enter it.

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog.git
cd vexy-co-model-catalog

  2. Create a virtual environment and install the package with the test and development extras.

    uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev,test]"

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
uv run python -m pytest -n auto

pyproject.toml sets -v --durations=10 -p no:briefcase as default options. To get a short summary, override them:

uv run python -m pytest -q -o addopts="" -n auto

Turn off analytics and the performance monitor while testing so the suite does not write into the repository:

VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED=false uv run python -m pytest -q -o addopts="" -n auto

The suite does not pass in full. A run on the current main branch gave 302 passed, 74 failed and 11 errors. Most failures are in the integrity, monitoring, production-diagnostics and quality-gate tests; tests/test_cli_smoke.py, tests/test_cli_optimization.py and tests/test_package.py pass except test_help_command.

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
The project uses Ruff. The pre-commit configuration runs ruff --fix, ruff-format and a set of whitespace and file checks.

uvx ruff check src tests
uvx ruff format --respect-gitignore src tests

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The version is derived from git tags by hatch-vcs. Tags have the form vX.Y.Z. At build time the version is written to src/vexy_co_model_catalog/_version.py, which is not tracked in git. Between tags the version looks like 1.0.5.dev0+g16e389c9f: the next patch version, a development counter and the commit.

When _version.py is missing (a plain checkout that was never built or installed), vexy_co_model_catalog.__version__ falls back to the installed distribution's metadata, then to 0.0.0.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
The root build.sh builds the documentation, the package, or both:

./build.sh            # docs and package
./build.sh docs       # src_docs/ → docs/
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, checked with twine

The source distribution contains the package, the tests, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE and pyproject.toml. The wheel contains the package only.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme. Sources are in src_docs/md/, the configuration in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

The build runs in strict mode, so a broken link or a page missing from the navigation stops it. The Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) rebuilds docs/ on every push to main that touches src_docs/ and commits the result.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Make sure the tests you care about pass and the docs build.
  2. Export a PyPI token for uv publish, for example UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.

  3. Run:

    ./publish.sh

    publish.sh runs gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes. It then builds the package from that tag and uploads it with uv publish.

Pushing the tag also starts the Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml). It builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with skip-existing, so a version already uploaded by publish.sh is not an error, and creates a GitHub release with the files attached.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer (requires-python = ">=3.10" in pyproject.toml).
  • Network access to the providers you want to query.
  • An API key for each provider that needs one. See Providers for the variable names.

The package depends on fire, httpx[http2], loguru, psutil, pyyaml, rich, tomli and tomli-w. The installer pulls them in.

docs.title: Install from GitHub
docs.text:
The package is not yet on PyPI. Install it straight from the repository.

uvpip 
uv tool install git+https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog

python -m pip install git+https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog

Both commands build the package from the latest commit. The version string comes from the nearest git tag, so a build made after v1.0.4 reports a version such as 1.0.5.dev0+g<commit>.

Once the package is on PyPI, the shorter form will work:

uv tool install vexy-co-model-catalog

docs.title: Install from a local checkout
docs.text:
Use this when you want to change the code or run the tests.

  1. Clone the repository.

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog.git
cd vexy-co-model-catalog

  2. Create a virtual environment and install the package in editable mode with the test extras.

    uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[test]"

  3. Check that the command runs.

    uv run vmc version

    The first line of the output names the package and its version, for example vexy-co-model-catalog version 1.0.5.dev0+g16e389c9f.

docs.title: Commands that get installed
docs.text:
The package installs two console scripts. Both run the same program.

Command Entry point vmc vexy_co_model_catalog.cli:main vexy-model-catalog vexy_co_model_catalog.cli:main

You can also run the module directly:

python -m vexy_co_model_catalog providers

Older examples

Earlier versions of the README used vexy-co-model-catalog as the command name. No script with that name is installed; use vmc or vexy-model-catalog.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
1. List the providers. This needs no network access.

    vmc providers

    The result is a table with 40 rows and the line Total: 40 providers configured.

  2. Check the configuration of one provider. This reads environment variables only.

    vmc validate openai

    The result ends with a Validation Summary block that counts valid and invalid providers.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
uvpip 
uv tool uninstall vexy-co-model-catalog

python -m pip uninstall vexy-co-model-catalog

Uninstalling does not remove files the tool wrote into your working directories (config/, models/, analytics/, performance/, .cache/vexy_model_catalog/). Delete those by hand if you no longer need them. Configuration lists what each one holds.

docs.title: Migrating from dump_models.py
docs.text: vexy-co-model-catalog replaces dump_models.py, a single script that fetched model lists from the same providers. A copy of that script is kept in the repository as external/dump_models.py for reference.

docs.title: What stays the same
docs.text:
• Provider names. The provider table is the same list of names, types, key variables and base-URL variables.
  • Environment variables. Keys are read from the same variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, HUGGINGFACEHUB_API_TOKEN, FRIENDLI_TOKEN, …), and base URLs from the same <NAME>_API_OPENAI variables.
  • File names. Output files are still called models_<provider>.json and models_<provider>.txt.
  • Re-running. Both tools skip a provider whose files already exist, unless you pass --force.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text: dump_models.py vmc Where files go The current directory, flat config/json/ and config/txt/ (or models/json/ and models/text/ with --legacy_output) TOML output models_<provider>.toml next to the others Not written Failure record failed_models.json in the current directory models/extra/failed_providers.json Skip check JSON, TXT and TOML files must all exist JSON and TXT files must both exist Retrying failed providers --failed_rescan vmc clean --failed, then fetch again Concurrency limit — --max_concurrency, default 8

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vmc is installed. See Installation.
  • Your API key variables are exported in the shell you use.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Change to the directory that holds your old models_*.json files.

    cd ~/models

  2. Optional: run the migration assistant. It needs a source checkout of the repository, because the assistant script is not part of the installed package.

    python /path/to/vexy-co-model-catalog/scripts/migrate_from_dump_models.py

    The assistant looks for models_*.json, models_*.txt and models_*.toml in ., models, ../models and ~/models. It prints how many providers and models it found, which of nine common key variables are set, and a suggested fetch command. It changes no files.

  3. Fetch fresh catalogs.

    vmc fetch

  4. Compare the new files with the old ones. Because the new files are sorted, sort the old ones the same way before you diff, or compare the TXT lists only:

    diff <(sort models_openai.txt) <(sort config/txt/models_openai.txt)

  5. Point your other tools at the new files. If they need the files flat in one directory, create links there:

    vmc link --target_dir=.

    This links ./models_<provider>.json and ./models_<provider>.txt to the files in config/. Existing files with those names are replaced by the links, so keep a copy of the old files first if you still need them.

  6. When the new files are in use, archive dump_models.py and the old failed_models.json.

docs.title: The migrate command
docs.text: vmc migrate runs the same assistant script. It looks for the script relative to the installed package, which only works when you run from a source checkout; an installed copy prints Migration script not found. The --search_paths argument is passed to the script as the SEARCH_PATHS variable, but the script does not read it in this version, so it always searches the four default locations listed above.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: vmc writes all its files below the directory you run it from. The storage root is the current working directory; there is no option to change it on the command line. In Python you can pass another root to StorageManager or ModelCatalog (see Python API).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
After vmc fetch openai and vmc fetch groq in an empty directory, the tree looks like this:

.
├── config/
│   ├── json/
│   │   ├── models_groq.json
│   │   └── models_openai.json
│   └── txt/
│       ├── models_groq.txt
│       └── models_openai.txt
├── models/
│   └── extra/
│       └── failed_providers.json
├── analytics/              # usage analytics, one JSON file per run
├── performance/            # performance monitor data
└── .cache/
    └── vexy_model_catalog/ # response cache

Directories are created the first time something is written to them.

Path Written by Content config/json/models_<provider>.json fetch The provider's response, sorted config/txt/models_<provider>.txt fetch One model ID per line config/aichat/models_<provider>.yaml fetch --output_config aichat client entry config/codex/models_<provider>.toml fetch --output_config codex profiles config/mods/models_<provider>.yml fetch --output_config mods API entry models/json/models_<provider>.json fetch --legacy_output Same as config/json/… models/text/models_<provider>.txt fetch --legacy_output Same as config/txt/… models/extra/failed_providers.json every fetch Failure tracker

docs.title: JSON files
docs.text:
The JSON file holds the provider's response after sorting, written with two-space indentation and UTF-8 characters kept as they are.

Sorting depends on the shape of the response:

  • {"data": [...]} (OpenAI style): the data array is sorted by each entry's id.
  • An object keyed by model ID (for example litellm): the keys are sorted.
  • A plain array: sorted by each entry's id.

Sorting makes two fetches of an unchanged catalog produce identical files, so you can keep them in git and read real changes from the diff.

docs.title: TXT files
docs.text:
The TXT file lists model IDs, one per line, in the same order as the JSON file, ending with a newline. For an object keyed by model ID, the key sample_spec is left out.

For litellm the file starts like this:

1024-x-1024/50-steps/bedrock/amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0
1024-x-1024/50-steps/stability.stable-diffusion-xl-v1
1024-x-1024/gpt-image-1.5
...

docs.title: How files are written
docs.text:
Every file is written atomically:

  1. The content goes to a temporary file in the target directory, named .<filename>.<random>.tmp.
  2. The temporary file is renamed over the target.

A reader therefore sees either the old file or the new one, never half a file. If the process is killed between the two steps, the temporary file stays behind; vmc clean --temp removes such files.

docs.title: The failure tracker
docs.text:
models/extra/failed_providers.json has one entry per provider that has been fetched:

{
  "litellm": {
    "consecutive_failures": 0,
    "errors": [],
    "failed": false,
    "failure_count": 0,
    "first_success": "2026-10-12T20:46:43.084930+00:00",
    "last_failure": null,
    "last_success": "2026-10-12T20:46:43.834184+00:00",
    "last_success_date": "Mon, 12 Oct 2026 20:46:43 GMT",
    "success_count": 2
  }
}
  • failed is true after a failed fetch and false after a successful one.
  • errors keeps the last 10 errors, each with a timestamp, the error message and the HTTP status_code.
  • vmc providers shows Failed for providers whose failed is true; vmc fetch --only_successful skips them.
  • vmc clean --failed resets the tracker.

docs.title: Tool config files
docs.text:
With --output_config, fetch also tries to write per-provider configuration snippets for three LLM command-line tools. Each snippet includes at most the first 5 model IDs, with max_input_tokens set to 8192 and max_output_tokens (or max_tokens) set to 4096, because the provider lists do not carry those limits.

aichat (YAML)codex (TOML)mods (YAML) 
groq:
  type: openai
  api_base: ...
  api_key: ${GROQ_API_KEY}
  models:
  - name: <model-id>
    max_input_tokens: 8192
    max_output_tokens: 4096

The type is claude for Anthropic providers and openai for all others.

[profiles.groq-<model-id>]
name = "groq-<model-id>"
base_url = "..."
api_key_env = "GROQ_API_KEY"
model = "<model-id>"
max_tokens = 4096
context_window = 8192

The profile name is <provider>-<model ID> with / and : replaced by -.

apis:
  groq:
    base_url: ...
    api_key: ${GROQ_API_KEY}
    models:
    - name: <model-id>
      provider: groq
      max_tokens: 4096

Each snippet is validated before it is written. A snippet with validation errors is not written; the run logs a warning such as Generated aichat config for groq has 1 errors - skipping write.

Config generation is unreliable in 1.0.x

The generators take the base URL from the provider's fixed base_url field, which the built-in providers leave empty (they use a base-URL variable instead). In a test run with vmc fetch litellm --force --output_config, no snippet was written: the mods generator failed with an internal error and the others did not produce a file. Treat --output_config as experimental. The JSON and TXT files are not affected.

The snippets are not merged into your real tool configuration. Earlier documentation described update-configs and generate-configs commands; they do not exist in this version.

docs.title: Legacy layout
docs.text:
--legacy_output writes the JSON and TXT files to models/json/ and models/text/ instead of config/json/ and config/txt/. The "files exist" check then looks in the legacy directories.

If a tool expects all files flat in one directory, use link instead. It creates links (or copies with --copy_files) named models_<provider>.json and models_<provider>.txt in one directory, models/ by default. See CLI reference.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: The provider list is fixed in code, in src/vexy_co_model_catalog/core/provider.py. It holds 40 providers. You cannot add or remove providers from the command line; vmc providers add and vmc providers remove only print a notice.

docs.title: Provider types
docs.text:
Each provider has one of three types. The type decides which URL is requested and how the API key is sent.

Type Request URL Authentication header openai <base URL>/models Authorization: Bearer <key> anthropic <base URL>/models x-api-key: <key> and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 url <base URL> itself none

Every request also carries User-Agent: ModelDumper/1.0.

docs.title: How the base URL is chosen
docs.text:
Each provider names two environment variables: one for the API key and one for the base URL.

  1. When the package loads the provider table, it sets each base-URL variable to its default value, unless that variable is already set in your environment.
  2. When a request is built, the tool reads the base-URL variable.

So you can point any provider at another endpoint by exporting its base-URL variable before you run vmc:

export LMSTUDIO_API_OPENAI="http://localhost:1234/v1"
vmc fetch lmstudio

The tool then requests http://localhost:1234/v1/models.

atlascloud has no default base URL

In the default URL table, the atlascloud entry is keyed ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY instead of ATLASCLOUD_API_OPENAI. As a result the package sets no default for ATLASCLOUD_API_OPENAI, and it also writes the URL into ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY when that variable is not already set. Set both variables yourself to use this provider:

export ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY="..."
export ATLASCLOUD_API_OPENAI="https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1"

lmstudio points at a local host name

The default for lmstudio is http://othello.local:1234/v1, a machine on the author's network. Plain http:// is only accepted for localhost and 127.0.0.1, so the default is rejected by the URL check. Set LMSTUDIO_API_OPENAI to your own server, for example http://localhost:1234/v1.

docs.title: Providers with special handling
docs.text: litellm A url provider. Its base URL is the JSON file model_prices_and_context_window.json in the LiteLLM repository, so no key is needed. The response is an object keyed by model ID; the sample_spec key is left out of the model ID list. chutes After the normal /models request, the tool also requests https://api.chutes.ai/chutes/?include_public=true&include_schemas=false and merges the extra fields into the matching model entries. If the second request fails, the tool logs a warning and keeps the first response. lmstudio The only provider in the table allowed to use plain http://, and only for localhost or 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: URL check
docs.text: Before each request the tool checks the URL. It must use https://; plain http:// is accepted only for localhost and 127.0.0.1, and only for lmstudio. Host names that contain patterns such as metadata, internal, private, 169.254 or 10. are rejected. A rejected URL fails the provider with a message that starts with SECURITY: URL failed security validation.

docs.title: Response formats
docs.text:
The tool accepts three response shapes and extracts model IDs from each:

Shape Example Model IDs taken from OpenAI style {"data": [{"id": "gpt-4o"}, …]} each data[].id; data is sorted by id Object keyed by ID {"gpt-4o": {…}, …} the keys, except sample_spec; keys are sorted Plain array [{"id": "gpt-4o"}, …] each id; the array is sorted by id

docs.title: Check a provider
docs.text:
vmc providers show groq      # type, key variable, base URL, failure stats
vmc validate groq            # is the key set? is a base URL available?
vmc provider_health groq     # does the endpoint answer?

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The package is vexy_co_model_catalog. Importing it is cheap: the top level exposes the version and two classes, and everything else lives in vexy_co_model_catalog.core.*.

import vexy_co_model_catalog

print(vexy_co_model_catalog.__version__)

The functions and classes on this page are the ones the CLI itself uses. They are not declared a stable public API; pin the package version if you build on them.

docs.title: Fetch one provider from Python
docs.text:
This example does what vmc fetch litellm does, step by step. It needs no API key.

import asyncio

from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.fetcher import ModelFetcher
from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.provider import get_provider_by_name
from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.storage import StorageManager


async def main() -> None:
    provider = get_provider_by_name("litellm")  # a "url" provider: no API key needed
    async with ModelFetcher(max_concurrency=4) as fetcher:
        data = await fetcher.fetch_provider_models(provider)
        data = fetcher.sort_json_data(data)
        model_ids = fetcher.extract_model_ids(data)

    storage = StorageManager("catalog")  # root directory for output
    storage.write_config_json("models_litellm", data)
    storage.write_config_txt("models_litellm", model_ids)
    print(f"{len(model_ids)} models, first: {model_ids[0]}")


asyncio.run(main())

4060 models, first: 1024-x-1024/50-steps/bedrock/amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0

The files land in catalog/config/json/models_litellm.json and catalog/config/txt/models_litellm.txt.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Module: vexy_co_model_catalog.core.provider

get_all_providers() -> list[ProviderConfig] Return the 40 built-in providers. As a side effect it sets each provider's base-URL environment variable to its default, unless the variable is already set. get_provider_by_name(name: str) -> ProviderConfig | None Return one provider, or None if the name is unknown. ProviderKind String enum with the values "openai", "anthropic" and "url". ProviderConfig

A dataclass describing one provider.

Field Type Default name str required kind ProviderKind required api_key_env str | None None base_url_env str | None None base_url str | None None headers dict[str, str] | None None timeout float 15.0 verify_ssl bool True

get_base_url() returns the value of base_url_env if that variable is set, otherwise base_url. build_models_url() returns the base URL itself for url providers and <base URL>/models for the others; it raises ValueError when there is no base URL.

You can describe a provider that is not in the table and fetch it the same way:

import os

from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.provider import ProviderConfig, ProviderKind

os.environ["MYHOST_API_KEY"] = "..."
provider = ProviderConfig(
    name="myhost",
    kind=ProviderKind.OPENAI,
    api_key_env="MYHOST_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://llm.example.com/v1",
)
print(provider.build_models_url())  # https://llm.example.com/v1/models

docs.title: Fetching
docs.text:
Module: vexy_co_model_catalog.core.fetcher

ModelFetcher(max_concurrency: int = 8, timeout: float = 30.0, failure_tracker: FailureTracker | None = None) An asynchronous HTTP client. Use it as an async context manager so its connection pool is closed. await fetcher.fetch_provider_models(provider, use_cache=True) Request the provider's model list and return the parsed JSON (dict or list). Retries with exponential back-off. Raises AuthenticationError on 401/403, RateLimitError on 429 and FetchError on other HTTP errors, invalid JSON or a URL that fails the URL check. When a failure_tracker is given, every outcome is recorded in it. fetcher.sort_json_data(data) Return the data sorted as described in Output files. fetcher.extract_model_ids(data) -> list[str] Return the model IDs.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Module: vexy_co_model_catalog.core.storage (also exported from vexy_co_model_catalog.core)

StorageManager(root_path=None) File storage below root_path, or below the current directory when root_path is None. All writes are atomic. Method Writes to write_config_json(name, data) <root>/config/json/<name>.json write_config_txt(name, lines) <root>/config/txt/<name>.txt write_json(name, data) <root>/models/json/<name>.json write_text(name, lines) <root>/models/text/<name>.txt write_yaml(name, data, directory=…) config/<name>.yaml, config/aichat/<name>.yaml or config/mods/<name>.yml write_config_toml(name, data) <root>/config/codex/<name>.toml

read_json(name, directory=…) reads back JSON from "json", "extra" or "config_json". list_files(directory, pattern="*") lists files in one of "json", "text", "extra", "config_json", "config_txt", "config_aichat", "config_codex", "config_mods". get_file_stats() returns a file count per directory.

docs.title: Catalog and registry
docs.text:
Exported from the top-level package.

ProviderRegistry() A name-to-ProviderConfig mapping. Methods: register(name, provider) (raises ValueError for an empty name or a non-ProviderConfig), get(name), get_required(name) (raises KeyError), list_names(), list_providers(), items(), contains(name), remove(name), clear(), count(). ModelCatalog(storage=None, registry=None, storage_root=None) Bundles a StorageManager and a ProviderRegistry. Missing parts are created. Methods: get_storage_root(), get_provider_count(), validate_configuration(); the last returns False when the storage root does not exist yet. 
from vexy_co_model_catalog import ModelCatalog
from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.provider import get_all_providers

catalog = ModelCatalog(storage_root="catalog")
for provider in get_all_providers():
    catalog.registry.register(provider.name, provider)

print(catalog.get_provider_count())                      # 40
print(catalog.registry.get_required("groq").api_key_env)  # GROQ_API_KEY

ModelCatalog does not fetch anything by itself. Use ModelFetcher and StorageManager as in the first example.

docs.title: Failure tracking
docs.text:
Module: vexy_co_model_catalog.core.failure_tracker

FailureTracker(storage: StorageManager) Reads and writes models/extra/failed_providers.json below the storage root. Methods include is_provider_failed(name), get_provider_failure_info(name), get_failed_providers(), get_failure_summary(), reset_provider_failures(name) and reset_all_failures(). 
from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.failure_tracker import FailureTracker
from vexy_co_model_catalog.core.storage import StorageManager

tracker = FailureTracker(StorageManager("catalog"))
print(tracker.get_failure_summary()["currently_failed"])

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
This page follows one provider through a complete run: check it, fetch it, look at the files, fetch it again, and link the results into a second directory.

The example uses the litellm provider because it needs no API key. Its "API" is a public JSON file in the LiteLLM repository that lists model prices and context windows. The steps are the same for any other provider once its API key is set.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vmc is installed. See Installation.
  • You have network access to raw.githubusercontent.com.

docs.title: 1. Make a working directory
docs.text:
vmc writes everything relative to the directory you run it from. Start in an empty one so you can see what appears.

mkdir catalog-demo
cd catalog-demo

docs.title: 2. Look at the provider
docs.text:
vmc providers show litellm

Provider: litellm
Type: url
API Key Env: None
Base URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json

Type: url means the base URL is the file to download; the tool does not append /models.

docs.title: 3. Check the configuration
docs.text:
vmc validate litellm

validate reads environment variables only; it sends no requests. For a provider that needs a key, this is where a missing …_API_KEY shows up.

docs.title: 4. Fetch the catalog
docs.text:
vmc fetch litellm

Fetching from 1 providers...
Using config/ directory structure
Validating provider configurations...
✓ All provider configurations valid
Processing litellm
✓ litellm: 4060 models

Fetch Complete: 1 successful, 0 failed, 0 skipped

The count was 4060 when this page was written; it changes as the upstream file changes.

docs.title: 5. Look at the files
docs.text:
find . -type f -path './config/*' -o -type f -path './models/*'

./config/json/models_litellm.json
./config/txt/models_litellm.txt
./models/extra/failed_providers.json

  • config/json/models_litellm.json holds the downloaded data. For litellm it is an object keyed by model ID, sorted by key:

    {
  "1024-x-1024/50-steps/bedrock/amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0": {
    "deprecation_date": "2026-09-30",
    "litellm_provider": "bedrock",
    "max_input_tokens": 2600,
    "mode": "image_generation",
    "output_cost_per_image": 0.06
  },

  • config/txt/models_litellm.txt holds one model ID per line, in the same order.

  • models/extra/failed_providers.json records that litellm succeeded. A later --only_successful run uses it to skip providers that failed.

The tool also creates analytics/, performance/ and .cache/vexy_model_catalog/ in the working directory. Configuration explains each and how to turn the first two off.

docs.title: 6. Run the fetch again
docs.text:
vmc fetch litellm

Processing litellm
Skipping litellm (files exist, use --force to overwrite)

Fetch Complete: 0 successful, 0 failed, 1 skipped

A provider is skipped when both its JSON file and its TXT file already exist. Add --force to write them again.

docs.title: 7. Link the files somewhere else
docs.text:
Some tools expect the files flat in one directory. link creates symbolic links to them:

vmc link

✓ litellm

Linked 2 files for 1 providers

The links land in models/ by default:

models/models_litellm.json -> …/catalog-demo/config/json/models_litellm.json
models/models_litellm.txt  -> …/catalog-demo/config/txt/models_litellm.txt

Use --target_dir to pick another directory and --copy_files to copy instead of linking. See CLI reference.

docs.title: 8. Fetch a provider that needs a key
docs.text:
1. Find the key variable in Providers. For Groq it is GROQ_API_KEY.

  2. Export the key.

    export GROQ_API_KEY="..."

  3. Fetch.

    vmc fetch groq

    If the key is missing, the validation step stops the provider before any request is sent:

    ✗ groq:
  • Environment variable GROQ_API_KEY is not set
...
No valid providers remaining after validation. Please fix configuration issues.

docs.title: 9. Fetch several providers at once
docs.text:
Pass the names as one comma-separated string. Because of how the command-line parser reads commas, wrap the list in two sets of quotes:

vmc fetch --providers='"openai,groq,mistral"'

Run vmc fetch with no provider to fetch every provider in the table. Providers whose key is not set fail validation and are dropped from the run; the others are fetched.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with these three commands. None of them changes your catalogs.

vmc version            # which version is running
vmc validate           # are the key variables set?
vmc providers          # which providers are marked Failed?

docs.title: TypeError: CLI.__init__() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given
docs.text: Every command fails with this error in version 1.0.4 and earlier. A wrapper around the CLI class hid its real signature from Fire, so Fire passed the command name to the constructor. Install a build newer than v1.0.4; see Installation.

docs.title: ImportError: Using http2=True, but the 'h2' package is not installed
docs.text:
fetch fails with this error in installs that lack the h2 package. The HTTP client is created with HTTP/2 enabled, which needs httpx[http2]. Newer builds declare that dependency. For an older install, add the package to the same environment:

python -m pip install h2

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psutil'
docs.text:
The environment was created from an outdated lock file. Install the package again so its declared dependencies are resolved, or add the module:

uv pip install psutil

docs.title: A traceback after --help
docs.text:
Fire passes --help to the command when it comes straight after it. Put -- in front:

vmc fetch -- --help

docs.title: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'split'
docs.text:
You passed several providers without the extra quotes. Fire turns openai,groq into a tuple. Quote the list twice:

vmc fetch --providers='"openai,groq"'

docs.title: Warning: Provider '<name>' not found
docs.text: The name is not in the provider table. Names are lower case and match the first column of vmc providers, for example togetherai (not together) and inference (not inferencenet).

docs.title: A provider is skipped or dropped
Skipping <provider> (files exist, use --force to overwrite)
docs.text:
Both config/json/models_<provider>.json and config/txt/models_<provider>.txt already exist. Add --force:

vmc fetch openai --force

docs.title: Environment variable <NAME> is not set
docs.text:
Validation found no API key. The provider is removed from the run before any request is sent. Look up the variable name in Providers and export it:

export GROQ_API_KEY="..."
vmc validate groq

docs.title: Skipped <n> failed providers
docs.text:
You used --only_successful, and the failure tracker has those providers marked as failed. Reset the tracker and try again:

vmc clean --failed
vmc fetch

docs.title: Authentication failed (401) or (403)
docs.text: The provider rejected the key. Check that the variable holds the right key for that provider and that the key is still active. The provider is now marked Failed in vmc providers; a successful fetch clears the mark.

docs.title: Rate limited
docs.text: The provider answered 429 Too Many Requests. Wait and try again, or fetch fewer providers at once with a lower --max_concurrency.

docs.title: SECURITY: URL failed security validation for <provider>
docs.text:
The base URL did not pass the URL check. The usual causes:

  • The URL uses http://. Only lmstudio may use http://, and only with localhost or 127.0.0.1.
  • The host name contains internal, private, metadata, 169.254 or 10..

Check the effective URL with vmc providers show <provider>, then fix the base-URL variable.

docs.title: No base URL configured for provider atlascloud
docs.text: The built-in table sets no default base URL for atlascloud. Export ATLASCLOUD_API_OPENAI yourself; see the note in Providers.

docs.title: Invalid JSON response from <provider>
docs.text: The endpoint answered with something other than JSON, often an HTML error page. Check the provider's status page and the base URL.

docs.title: Files are not where you expect
docs.text: vmc writes into the directory you run it from. If you ran it from your home directory, the catalogs are in ~/config/json/ and ~/config/txt/. Pick one directory for the catalogs and always cd there first, as in the scheduled-run example in Configuration.

docs.title: analytics/ and performance/ folders appear everywhere
docs.text:
They come from usage analytics and the performance monitor, which are on by default. Turn them off:

export VEXY_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false
export VEXY_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED=false

docs.title: --output_config writes nothing
docs.text: Tool config generation does not work reliably in 1.0.x; see the warning in Output files. The JSON and TXT catalogs are written regardless.

docs.title: Migration script not found
docs.text: vmc migrate only works from a source checkout. Run the script directly instead; see Migrating from dump_models.py.

docs.title: In-app help mentions commands that do not exist
docs.text: vmc help and some error messages mention generate-configs, backup-configs, restore-configs, and the fetch flags --verbose, --timeout and --use-cache. None of these exist in this version. Older copies of the README also mention update-configs, which does not exist either. The commands and flags that do exist are listed in CLI reference, and vmc <command> -- --help shows the real flags of any command.
